## Schedule I 0.4.7 support

- Updates both dedicated hosts and companion clients for the released Special Customers update, on Mono (`alternate`) and IL2CPP (`public`). Player identity/loading, time, messaging, NPC movement, police response, and avatar integration use the current native APIs.
- Migrates sleeping to `SleepController` and `SleepMenu`. Headless event queues retain gameplay and special-customer events while skipping interactive screens; consumed readiness votes cannot repeatedly advance days while clients dismiss summaries.
- Resolves special-customer IDs using their asset spelling, including first-visit selection and existing mixed-case save IDs.
- Avoids headless reflection blending, weather-mask rendering, GPU instancing, and light-culling work. Pooled NPC weather actions wait until character data exists.
- Uses the native rotation-aware teleport overload and current runtime icon-generation patch target. These fix final-release compilation and Harmony startup failures. See [PR #69](https://github.com/ifBars/S1DedicatedServers/pull/69).

## Compatibility and validation

Existing public mod signatures, configuration, save identities, and network payload formats are preserved. Update the server and clients together and use the matching runtime/role package. This release targets Schedule I 0.4.7.

All four final 0.4.7f12 configurations build with zero warnings and errors. Sleep-controller and special-customer regression checks pass. Both final-release headless servers load a disposable save without Harmony patch failures; an external client per runtime passes two connect/rejoin cycles, with join/leave autosaves and authoritative quest replay. TCP console information, time changes, manual saving, and graceful shutdown pass on both runtimes.

These local checks used Tugboat, a Steam emulator, and disabled authentication/mod verification. WAN connectivity, real Steam authentication, f12 sleep transitions with external clients, and third-party mod combinations were not tested in this pass. Transient reconnect menu-setup warnings and native headless graphics warnings remain.
